note: Two blobs on one record. A record carries at most one file in 0.2; `blobs` is an array so that several is a later minor version, not something a host may accept today without a sealed body that can describe more than one file.

An empty `blobs` array. A record with no file omits the member; an empty array would be a second spelling of absence that a host and a producer could disagree about when deciding whether a rewrite releases the previous version's blob.

A blob named by a bare hex SHA-256 rather than a multibase multihash. A BlobRef is self-describing so that the hash can change without a schema revision; a hex string hard-codes one algorithm into the wire contract.

The file's manifest sent in the clear beside the record. Everything that describes a file is sealed inside the record body, signed by its author; the host gets only the reference, and an unknown member is refused rather than stored.
No presentation. Authority comes from the room's own credentials on every write; a host never authorizes from a session or a list of its own.
